results.title: Ahmedabad's Cricket Ticket Frenzy: A Systemic Issue | Rushabh Shah posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.snippet: For a true cricket fan, the real World Cup final happens before the match: getting a ticket. #Ahmedabad has now hosted some of the biggest matches in world cricket - World Cup clashes, IPL finals, and now the 2026 T20 World Cup Final. But there is one pattern that keeps repeating. > Tickets open. > Tickets disappear within minutes. > And soon after, they appear in the black market at multiples of the original price. This has been happening repeatedly. ▶️ 2023 ODI World Cup Final – India vs [...] reaching 4 - 6x At this point, calling it “mismanagement” feels too simplistic. It looks more like a structural flaw in ticket distribution. I do not know what is holding it back, but it seems like ICC, BCCI, or BookMyShow wants to keep on doing it. Because when a 132,000-seat stadium sells out instantly every single time, the obvious question becomes: "How many tickets actually reach genuine fans?" If Ahmedabad is positioning itself as a global destination for marquee cricket events, the [...] Final – India vs Australia Probably the biggest cricket match India has hosted in decades. And the ticket frenzy was unprecedented. • Tickets originally priced in the ₹2,000 – ₹10,000 range • Black market quotes reportedly reaching ₹50,000 to ₹2 lakh • Multiple incidents of fake and duplicate tickets being circulated For a stadium that can hold 132,000 people, thousands of genuine fans couldn’t get access. ▶️ India vs Pakistan – World Cup 2023 The same pattern emerged. • Tickets resold at 10x

results.snippet: The Narendra Modi Stadium (formerly known as Motera Stadium) is a cricket stadium situated in Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Sports Complex, Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. It is the largest stadium in the world, with a seating capacity of 132,000 spectators. The stadium is owned by the Gujarat Cricket Association and serves as a venue for Test, ODI, T20I, FC, List-A, T20 and Indian Premier League cricket matches. The stadium was constructed in 1983 and was first renovated in 2006. It became the regular [...] became the regular venue for international matches in the city. In 2015, the stadium was closed and demolished before being completely rebuilt by February 2020, with an estimated cost of ₹800 crore (US$100 million). Apart from cricket, the stadium has hosted several programs arranged by the Government of Gujarat. It has hosted matches during the 1987, 1996, and 2011 Cricket World Cups. As of 2022, the stadium has hosted 14 Tests, 27 ODIs, 6 T20s matches and 2 IPL matches On 24 February 2021, [...] 24 February 2021, the stadium was renamed as the Narendra Modi Stadium by the Gujarat Cricket Association after the current Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi, a Gujarat native, who was also the president of Gujarat Cricket Association (2009–2014) and the chief minister of the state from 2001 - 2014. It hosted its first ever pink ball test match on 24 February 2021 between India and England. The arena will host the final of the 2023 ICC World Cup on 19 November.
